comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C89-C93 regarding full-length BRAF validation. Both evaluations support that NT constructs recapitulate FL-BRAF behavior with similar KRAS binding affinities, validating the fragment-based approach.

Strong agreement on claims C100-C107 regarding CRD-KD interactions and BSR's role in stabilizing them. Both evaluations support the pulldown and OpenSPR data showing CRD is necessary for KD binding and BSR increases affinity.

Strong agreement on claims C113-C116 regarding RAS-mediated relief of autoinhibition. Both evaluations support the finding that HRAS abolishes NT1-KD autoinhibitory interactions, representing a key mechanistic insight.

Strong agreement on claims C58-C60 regarding pulldown validation experiments. Both evaluations support these as control experiments validating differential binding of active vs inactive HRAS. Peer review also includes C82 from a related validation experiment.

Strong agreement on claims C121-C123 regarding D594G mutation effects. Both evaluations support that this oncogenic mutation destabilizes autoinhibitory interactions, though both note the mechanistic inference could benefit from additional validation.

Strong agreement on claims C61-C69 regarding HDX-MS data showing RBD as main HRAS mediator and conformational changes in BSR. Peer review also includes C94-C96 about differential KRAS vs HRAS effects on BSR, which OpenEval addresses separately in R7.

Strong agreement on claims C75-C78 regarding the unusual finding that NT1 (BSR+RBD+CRD) does not bind HRAS at standard flow rates. Both evaluations support this as central to understanding BSR's negative regulatory role and isoform specificity mechanism.

Strong agreement on the integrative claims C5, C124, C136 regarding BSR-mediated isoform specificity. Both evaluations support that BSR provides an additional layer of autoinhibitory constraint and mediates differential KRAS vs HRAS binding. Peer review also includes C57, C79, C97 as supporting evidence.

Strong agreement on claims C70-C73 regarding OpenSPR-derived KD values for HRAS binding to various BRAF constructs. Both evaluations support these as novel quantitative measurements. Peer review groups these with C83-C86 (KRAS binding data), which OpenEval addresses separately in R5.

Partial overlap on claims C83-C86 regarding KRAS isoform specificity measurements. OpenEval R5 covers C82-C88 focusing on isoform specificity mechanism, while peer R3 groups KRAS data (C83-C86) with HRAS data (C70-C73) as part of the novel KD measurements.

Partial overlap on claims C94-C96 regarding differential HDX-MS effects of KRAS vs HRAS on BSR structure. OpenEval R7 focuses on these as mechanistic insight into isoform specificity, while peer R2 groups them with general HDX-MS findings (C61-C69).
Agreement on claim C133 regarding novelty of reporting first KD values for BRAF N- and C-terminal interactions. Both evaluations acknowledge this as a novel contribution to the field.

OpenEval R14 evaluates claims C68-C69 regarding AlphaFold predictions as UNCERTAIN due to lower confidence for disordered regions. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; peer reviewers did not specifically address the reliability of AlphaFold-based interpretations.

OpenEval R15 evaluates claims C128-C130 regarding SEC validation of oligomeric states as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; peer reviewers did not specifically comment on these validation experiments.

OpenEval R16 evaluates claims C1-C57, C98-C99, C117-C120, C131-C132 as SUPPORTED background/literature claims. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; peer reviewers focused on novel findings rather than evaluating background claims.

Minimal overlap on claim C112. OpenEval R9 covers C108-C112 regarding minimal RAP1A binding and inference that RBD+CRD are essential. Peer R4 mentions C112 in context of CRD-KD interactions but does not specifically evaluate the RAP1A experiments.
Peer R5 evaluates claim C137 (RAS-mediated relief of autoinhibition) which is not explicitly listed in OpenEval results, though the concept is covered in OpenEval R10's evaluation of C113-C116.
Peer R6 evaluates claim C138 (D594G mutation and oncogenic potential) which is not explicitly listed in OpenEval results, though the concept is covered in OpenEval R11's evaluation of C121-C123.
